comments.text: Only one person didn’t tip her.  That’s amazing because MOST people don’t tip anything, even when they order over $100 worth of food from Red Lobster, Mr & Mrs Crab, etc.  This is why so many of us have quit doing food deliveries, especially with the price of gas now and the other increases in car maintenance.  Many of us have been priced out of the second jobs we need to keep a roof over our heads and food for our own children.  And no, we don’t have someone else bring it to us.  People feel extremely entitled to not appreciate others who are doing work for their benefit by giving them at least some kind of tip.  To me, the tip should be based on how far away the restaurant is rather than the order amount because people will often order 1 boba tea, one piece of cheesecake, etc. from over 15 miles away, 30 miles round trip!  The order time is only changed when the restaurant is late filling the order.  However, the delivery company should refund the customer, pay the driver for their time as a “cost of doing business”, especially if they keep the customer updated in the app and refuse to pay the restaurant if the delay is their fault.  The apps are getting worse too because the IT department has to justify their jobs by making unnecessary, detrimental changes.  I don’t agree with people stealing as a way to make up for not being tipped though.  I just quit working for a company that caters to ungrateful people who don’t care about their fellow human beings.

comments.text: You have to make at least $1/mile, including the trip to the next pickup.  To pay your bills you need make at least $200, which is 200 miles.  A day.  If you had a normal job, that would be about 20 miles a day.  About ten times less miles per day.  So you can expect every part in your car to wear out 10x faster.  Brakes, suspension, engine, transmission, everything.  For that and gas, it is smart to say that your overhead is at least $5 per hour.  So you need to be making $30 an hour for it to be even worth it.  But the vast majority of trips are way less than $1.00 a mile.   Other than local food orders that are like 2 miles and take an hour because of traffic etc.   The whole thing is really a scam that makes it look  like it pays way more than it actually does.  It is something people do on the side to make a little extra money in the short term.  If you rely on it for more than that you are going to have major financial problems unless you live in one of a few markets that actually work well.  Eg doing spark in a rural area where 90% of each trip is highway and every order is at least $30 and takes 30-40 minutes, and rent is like 800 for a three bedroom house.

comments.author: @Vichedges
comments.text:
I honestly don't understand how Doordash has not been sued to oblivion yet.  Their business practices are so shady and just get worse and worse.

I've been Doordashing for about a year and a half and incrementally DD has just made it worse and worse for drivers as they try to squeeze every last dollar out of us.

They hired drivers nonstop for months and then got rid of scheduling in my area so the market is now flooded with drivers at all times.  My first year you had to schedule so if there were too many drivers you just couldn't dash.  But since they don't pay us they don't care if drivers sit around all night as long as the orders are getting delivered by someone. Whether there's 10 drivers or 10,000 doesn't make any difference to Doordash.

They got rid of driver scheduling and they stacked more and more offers together.  What they do is they hide no tip or low tip offers by pairing them with decent offers.  But they only pay the driver 1 delivery fee for stacked offers, which makes zero sense.  It's still two pickups and two deliveries

 Why would anyone ever take a $2 offer?  Doordash shouldn't even be sending that garbage to drivers unless they're EBT  but they send it then punish you by lowering your ratings if you don't accept it.

comments.text:
Your country is so fucked up right now. What strikes me most, as someone from the Netherlands, is the domino effect.

Big companies lay people off, and suddenly they’re left struggling to survive with very little support. So they turn to Uber, Uber Eats, DoorDash, or whatever gig work they can find just to make ends meet.
At the same time, groceries, gas, rent, and everyday expenses keep getting more expensive. People cut back on things like eating out, which then hurts restaurants and their employees as well. One problem creates the next. And meanwhile, CEOs and shareholders continue to make millions while ordinary working people are being squeezed harder and harder. 

As a Dutch person looking at this from the outside, it’s honestly difficult to comprehend how this can continue.
